subject: Throughput & streaming inquiry — Logistiq pilot
messages:
From: Evan Mercer <evan@logistiq.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Intro: throughput & streaming Qs for Logistiq pilot

Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary of our requirements so we have a single source of truth:

- Goal: pilot Redwood inference for live order-tracking chatbot (customer-facing)
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for 512-token average responses (interactive use)
- Streaming: required — we need partial token streaming to render interim text
- Concurrency: expect 80–150 simultaneous client streams in peak windows (conservative 120)
- QPS: steady-state 4–6 qps, peak sustained 35–45 qps for bursts (~20–30 minute windows)
- Token shapes: avg response ~420 tokens; inbound prompts ~60 tokens; estimated tokens/sec at peak ~ (45 qps * 480 tokens) ~= 21.6k tokens/sec
- Persistence/retention: short-term logs only; KV cache safe to keep for 30 minutes

Can you confirm if these numbers map to Dedicated sizing we discussed, and what the recommended canary looks like? I can share a small sample of recent request traces (sanitized) if helpful.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Mercer
Head of Platform
Logistiq

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Mercer <evan@logistiq.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: throughput & streaming Qs for Logistiq pilot

Evan —

Appreciate the clear summary. High-level read:

- Latency p95 300ms for ~512 tokens is achievable but depends on model choice (we'll validate—gpt-eco-like variants vs higher-capacity models) and streaming implementation. Streaming adds head-of-line token emission constraints.
- The concurrency/peak QPS numbers imply ~20k–25k tokens/sec sustained during peaks; we'll need to size for that plus a 20% headroom for burstiness and retries.

Action items / next steps:
1) Evan: please send a 1k-sample of sanitized request/response pairs and a representative traffic curve (CSV or JSONL). (attachment stub: logistiq_sla_needs.xlsx)
2) Redwood: Soojin + Marissa to draft a provisional throughput map (tokens/sec -> GPU pool estimate) and a short canary plan (duration, target windows, success criteria).
3) Align on streaming semantics (KV cache retention, partial-response latency SLOs) in follow-up engineering call.

Tentative timing: we can get the sizing map to you by EOD Monday if we have the samples by EOD today.

I'll loop in engineering for a technical deep-dive once we have the samples.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: throughput & streaming Qs for Logistiq pilot — sizing assumptions

Team —

I sketched a quick set of assumptions to use in the provisional sizing map. Please call out any corrections before we send to Logistiq:

- Avg response tokens: 420 (use 480 for peak-window safety)
- Inbound token avg: 60
- Streaming adds ~40–80ms to first-byte for large models; we assume optimizations can get that under 100ms for early tokens
- Target headroom: +20% tokens/sec to cover retries and client reconnects
- Concurrency vs QPS: concurrency 120 at peak maps to ~0.4s avg think-time per client during streaming; treat concurrency numbers as simultaneous active streams, not queued connections

Proposed test plan (canary):
- 60-minute rolling window; ramp to 50% of peak for first 15 minutes, 100% for next 30, then ramp down
- Real-time telemetry: token rate, p50/p95 latency, streaming bytes/time, error-rate
- Success criteria: p95 latency within 15% of target and error-rate <0.5%

Questions for Logistiq to confirm:
- Are there heavy multimodal payloads (images) in the pilot? (affects tokens/sec and memory)
- Any regional constraints? (we assume us-east primary)

I'll prepare a simple mapping table (tokens/sec -> GPU instance types + estimated QPS) — will attach to the Monday draft.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intro: throughput & streaming Qs for Logistiq pilot — answers + canary

Jordan / Soojin —

Thanks — sending the sanitized sample payloads now (attachment: sample_payloads.jsonl). Quick answers:

- No images or multimodal content in the pilot.
- Region: us-east preferred, with eu-west as fallback for EU traffic.
- We can commit to the 60-minute canary window next Tuesday; prefer the 14:00–15:00 UTC slot.
- We're interested in an estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted (cost delta and latency expectations); please include quantization support as an option.

We expect to provide the sample traces and traffic curve before EOD today.

Confirming next call: Tuesday 14:00 UTC for canary run kickoff.

— Evan
Evan Mercer
Head of Platform, Logistiq
